english: Let $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{100}$ be an increasing arithmetic progression such that $a_4+a_{12}=50$ and $a_3a_{13}=400$, and let $b_1,b_2,\dots,b_{100}$ be an arithmetic progression such that $b_2+b_{18}=100$ and $b_5+b_6+b_7=90$. The numbers that are terms of both progressions are written as $c_1<c_2<\dots<c_m$. Then the value of $\dfrac{c_1+c_2+\cdots+c_m}{m}$ is ______.
hindi: माना $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{100}$ एक वर्धमान समान्तर श्रेढ़ी है जिसके लिए $a_4+a_{12}=50$ तथा $a_3a_{13}=400$ है, तथा $b_1,b_2,\dots,b_{100}$ एक समान्तर श्रेढ़ी है जिसके लिए $b_2+b_{18}=100$ तथा $b_5+b_6+b_7=90$ है। जो संख्याएँ दोनों श्रेढ़ियों के पद हैं, उन्हें $c_1<c_2<\dots<c_m$ के रूप में लिखा जाता है। तब $\dfrac{c_1+c_2+\cdots+c_m}{m}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Terms equidistant from a middle term: $a_4+a_{12}=2a_8\Rightarrow a_8=25$; $a_3a_{13}=(25-5d)(25+5d)=400\Rightarrow d^2=9,\ d=3$
Common terms: $\equiv1\pmod3$ and $\equiv0\pmod5\Rightarrow\equiv10\pmod{15}$, between $10$ and $301$: $10,25,\dots,295$, an AP with $m=20$
solution_full: In an arithmetic progression $a_p+a_q=2a_r$ whenever $p+q=2r$. So $a_4+a_{12}=2a_8=50$ and $a_8=25$.
With common difference $d$: $a_3=25-5d$ and $a_{13}=25+5d$, so $a_3a_{13}=625-25d^2=400$, $d^2=9$; the progression is increasing, so $d=3$.
Then $a_n=a_8+3(n-8)=3n+1$, so the first progression is $4,7,10,\dots,301$.
Similarly $b_2+b_{18}=2b_{10}=100$ gives $b_{10}=50$, and $b_5+b_6+b_7=3b_6=90$ gives $b_6=30$. The common difference is $\dfrac{50-30}{4}=5$, so $b_n=5n$: $5,10,\dots,500$.
A common term $c$ satisfies $c\equiv1\pmod 3$ and $c\equiv0\pmod 5$, that is, $c\equiv10\pmod{15}$; it must also lie in $[4,301]\cap[5,500]=[5,301]$.

Every number $\equiv10\pmod{15}$ in this range is a term of both progressions, so the common terms are $10,25,40,\dots,295$, an arithmetic progression with common difference $15$ and $m=\dfrac{295-10}{15}+1=20$ terms.
For an arithmetic progression, sum $=\dfrac m2(c_1+c_m)$, so the mean is $\dfrac{c_1+c_m}{2}=\dfrac{10+295}{2}=152.5$.
originality_note: New: both progressions are given only through operations on their terms (sums of equidistant terms and a product symmetric about a middle term), and the asked quantity is the mean of the common terms (way 5: operations on AP terms linked with common terms). Closest known: 'common terms of two listed APs' exercises. Different because: neither progression is written down; each must first be decoded from symmetric-term conditions, one of them through a difference of squares.

concept_use.Arithmetic Progression (AP) & Sum of AP: Both progressions are rebuilt as a_n = 3n + 1 and b_n = 5n, and the mean of an AP of common terms is (first + last)/2.
concept_use.Common terms of 2 or more Aps: The common terms are the numbers = 10 (mod 15) in the overlap [5, 301]; they form an AP with difference lcm(3, 5) = 15.
concept_use.Operations on terms of an AP: a_4 + a_12 = 2a_8, b_2 + b_18 = 2b_10, b_5 + b_6 + b_7 = 3b_6 and a_3 a_13 = a_8^2 - 25d^2 decode the conditions.
